summary: The manuscript reports a well‑specified, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics and archives the execution artifacts. The confirmatory result (no discordant pairs; paired difference = 0.0) is artifact‑grounded and the experimental bookkeeping appears consistent. However three previously identified required manuscript defects remain and must be corrected before finalisation: (1) the Disclosure Statement must be condensed to the single mandatory master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 and a concise prose summary (remove enumerated run‑level artifact listings); (2) at least one Related‑Work claim overstates empirical support and must be corrected or weakened to match the supplied verified bibliographic records; and (3) Methods must include an explicit sentence stating that execution/model_configuration.json records temperature=null, that null/unset temperature does not imply deterministic sampling, and that the adapter produced exactly one sampled generation per pair reused under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement still enumerates archived artifacts instead of being condensed to the single required master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 plus a concise summary of models/adapters/validator/preregistration/autonomy boundary (remove run‑level file paths, per‑file hashes, provider‑call filenames, and internal log listings from the prose).

A Related‑Work claim (that generate→validate→repair pipelines have been shown empirically to improve safety/repairability) is not supported by the verified bibliographic records provided; the in‑text claim must be corrected or weakened to match what the supplied citations actually support.

Methods lacks the explicit statement that (i) execution/model_configuration.json records temperature=null, (ii) null/unset temperature is not evidence of deterministic model sampling (it does not imply temperature=0), and (iii) the adapter produced exactly one sampled generation per pair that was reused under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement so it contains exactly one archived master‑prompt locator and its SHA‑256 (provenance/master_prompt.txt + SHA‑256) verbatim, plus a concise prose summary naming the LLM used (gpt‑5‑mini), adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the preregistration id (autocand_A1_prereg_v1), and a brief autonomy‑boundary statement; remove any enumerated run‑level file paths, per‑file hashes, provider‑call filenames, or internal log listings from the manuscript prose (archival artifact availability may remain documented in the archived bundle but not listed in the Disclosure).

Edit Related Work to ensure each empirical claim is supported by a verified citation from the supplied terminal_bibliographic_records. In particular, for the sentence claiming that generate→validate→repair pipelines have been shown empirically to improve safety/repairability, either (a) replace the claim with a supported statement that the approach is advocated or has been applied in adjacent domains and cite the appropriate verified records, or (b) supply a different verified record from the archived evidence that directly supports the empirical assertion. Do not add new external citations not already present in the evidence bundle; weaken the claim if necessary to match available records.

Add one explicit sentence in Methods stating: (i) the archived model_configuration.json records temperature=null, (ii) null/unset temperature should not be interpreted as evidence of deterministic model sampling (it does not imply temperature=0), and (iii) per the preregistered and executed adapter settings the pipeline produced exactly one sampled generation per pair which was reused by both baseline and guarded arms under shared_initial_candidate semantics (restate that no claim of deterministic model sampling is being made).
optional_revisions: Optionally report the task‑difficulty label counts (extreme: 40, very_hard: 160) in a single line in Methods with a pointer to the archived task_manifest.jsonl to help readers assess task mix.

Optionally add 1–2 concise sentences in Discussion proposing a concrete follow‑up preregistered design (e.g., independent two‑call per‑pair regime with estimated model_call budget) to guide readers who wish to avoid the ceiling effect while staying within practical budgets.
Optionally remove long representative JSON excerpts from the main prose and rely on the archived artifact bundle, improving information density and readability.
